vo-d04c3097a4.speaker: VO
vo-d04c3097a4.text: Thursday. The first snow of the year was coming down on Doyers Street like it hadn't been told about the Depression.

vo-c01f513731.speaker: VO
vo-c01f513731.text: I'd slept at the desk again. The desk didn't mind. The desk was paid for.

vo-4ea4daca12.speaker: VO
vo-4ea4daca12.text: Nothing there but dust, and the dust is mine.

vo-8a8bebd0b3.speaker: VO
vo-8a8bebd0b3.text: Seen it. Didn't help then either.

vo-494d807d90.speaker: VO
vo-494d807d90.text: If that was a clue, I'd have spotted it years ago.

vo-1fb8ed1058.speaker: VO
vo-1fb8ed1058.text: I've got bigger problems than that.

vo-128b85b93d.speaker: VO
vo-128b85b93d.text: An envelope, pushed under the door. Nobody slides good news under a door.

vo-a4b46ac0ca.speaker: VO
vo-a4b46ac0ca.text: Love letter from the landlord. He always writes when the money's late.

vo-1bbb6d71c8.speaker: VO
vo-1bbb6d71c8.text: Fifty dollars by Saturday, or "vacate the premises". Lee Wing writes a nice formal English when he's annoyed.

vo-1f751d646b.speaker: VO
vo-1f751d646b.text: Fifty dollars. I had a dollar and change, a hat, and a talent for finding things other people had lost.

vo-44e31d7318.speaker: VO
vo-44e31d7318.text: Pete would know who'd lost something this week. Pete always knows.

vo-58a86ba371.speaker: VO
vo-58a86ba371.text: M. LONG, INVESTIGATIONS. Painted backwards from in here, like most of my life.

vo-9069554170.speaker: VO
vo-9069554170.text: Somebody's slid something under it. Somebody wants it read before I go.

vo-ecb418b667.speaker: VO
vo-ecb418b667.text: My desk. Most of my clients have only ever seen the front of it.

vo-605fe06f41.speaker: VO
vo-605fe06f41.text: Top drawer: string, a broken pencil, and Natalia.

vo-1f47d086d7.speaker: VO
vo-1f47d086d7.text: Her photo, face-down, the way I keep it. Some cases you close. Some you just stop looking at.

vo-57d592b727.speaker: VO
vo-57d592b727.text: Empty. The bottle, I mean. The day's still got some fight in it.

vo-f5aa1858fd.speaker: VO
vo-f5aa1858fd.text: I shook it, in case it had changed its mind. It hadn't.

vo-2255419f02.speaker: VO
vo-2255419f02.text: The Bloody Angle. Tong men used to shoot each other round that bend. Now it's mostly laundry.

vo-cbbc102f22.speaker: VO
vo-cbbc102f22.text: First snow. By noon it'd be grey slush, same as everything else on this street.

vo-d7d2107013.speaker: VO
vo-d7d2107013.text: The blinds cut the morning into strips. It's easier to take that way.

vo-fbe7847911.speaker: VO
vo-fbe7847911.text: The radio. Dance bands in the morning, bad news by night.

vo-87516d310c.speaker: VO
vo-87516d310c.text: A dance band, playing like nobody had told them about the bread lines either.

vo-eed8c3b585.speaker: VO
vo-eed8c3b585.text: Old cases. String and photographs. Every one of them paid less than it cost.

vo-66418ab51a.speaker: VO
vo-66418ab51a.text: Nothing new to pin up. That's the trouble with nothing new.

vo-1ecaa69d67.speaker: VO
vo-1ecaa69d67.text: An NYPD commendation, 1924. They give you a frame while you're useful.

vo-854e775652.speaker: VO
vo-854e775652.text: A licence to investigate, issued by the State of New York. It doesn't say what.

vo-41308166c9.speaker: VO
vo-41308166c9.text: The telephone. The phone company and I aren't speaking.

vo-00a58c2b9a.speaker: VO
vo-00a58c2b9a.text: The sofa. A client's chair when there are clients. My bed when there aren't.

vo-261572c969.speaker: VO
vo-261572c969.text: The radiator knocks twice a day. It's the only thing in here that works for nothing.

vo-bc628208bf.speaker: VO
vo-bc628208bf.text: The spare hat. In my line you go through hats.

vo-7a5d532cba.speaker: VO
vo-7a5d532cba.text: My good coat. It's the one with the lining.

vo-b3181070d3.speaker: VO
vo-b3181070d3.text: Butts, no cigarettes. Story of my week.

vo-7c134f39e8.speaker: VO
vo-7c134f39e8.text: Closed cases, open bills. The cabinet doesn't care which drawer is which.

vo-de65d00868.speaker: VO
vo-de65d00868.text: A note to myself: "Pay the rent." I've been meaning to read it.

vo-a1dbf566f7.speaker: VO
vo-a1dbf566f7.text: The bulb thought about it and decided against.

vo-0014c12fa2.speaker: VO
vo-0014c12fa2.text: Brown paint over green paint over a hundred years of tenants.

vo-13bb5891e1.speaker: VO
vo-13bb5891e1.text: The building creaks. It's been holding its breath since 1890.

vo-47639391b4.speaker: VO
vo-47639391b4.text: Pete and Kate's place. You can hear the percolator from here, and Pete over the percolator.

vo-212f662c70.speaker: VO
vo-212f662c70.text: Number twelve. My office, my bedroom, my address for another two days.

vo-51175bcd10.speaker: VO
vo-51175bcd10.text: Nothing in there but the rent I don't have.

vo-75dd72ac71.speaker: VO
vo-75dd72ac71.text: The stairs down to Doyers Street. Forty-one of them. I've counted, on bad nights.

vo-3dfdf96aeb.speaker: VO
vo-3dfdf96aeb.text: Not yet. Pete hears things before the police do. I'll start next door.

vo-57acf49bf0.speaker: VO
vo-57acf49bf0.text: The Evening Clarion. Pete brings it home every night and reads his own byline like it's a love letter.

vo-b53ff15967.speaker: VO
vo-b53ff15967.text: Somebody's milk. In this building, that's practically a safe deposit.

vo-a02890d0f1.speaker: VO
vo-a02890d0f1.text: One bare bulb for the whole landing. Lee Wing believes in thrift. Other people's.

pete-e2e465ea90.speaker: PETE
pete-e2e465ea90.text: Coffee's on me. Technically it's on Kate. Don't tell Kate.

kate-d5d19e40f1.speaker: KATE
kate-d5d19e40f1.text: Kate can hear you, Peter. Kate is four feet away.

vo-41e7cd813c.speaker: VO
vo-41e7cd813c.text: The coffee was Kate's, the hangover was Pete's, and I'd brought my own.

vo-199cac4781.speaker: VO
vo-199cac4781.text: Pete's mess on one side, Kate's order on the other. The border's under constant negotiation.

vo-f84ac5421e.speaker: VO
vo-f84ac5421e.text: Everything in here's either filed or on the floor.

vo-7183aa30a0.speaker: VO
vo-7183aa30a0.text: Kate would know. Kate always knows.

vo-9c7975a252.speaker: VO
vo-9c7975a252.text: The percolator. The hardest-working thing in this flat, and that includes Kate.

vo-4f06ed6452.speaker: VO
vo-4f06ed6452.text: I poured myself a cup. It tasted like somebody else's rent money.

vo-8db6aa3f5b.speaker: VO
vo-8db6aa3f5b.text: Pete's cigarettes. Right there on the table, where Kate can watch them.

vo-b89250fd36.speaker: VO
vo-b89250fd36.text: Pete's typewriter. He's got his back to it. That's how Pete writes: facing the room, in case something happens.

vo-44fd8f71c0.speaker: VO
vo-44fd8f71c0.text: Pete's clippings. Every crime on the Lower East Side since 1927, and a few he only hoped for.

vo-45f1fd1306.speaker: VO
vo-45f1fd1306.text: Kate's ledgers. Neat columns. Kate's the only person I know whose sums come out the same twice.

vo-a17ee6241c.speaker: VO
vo-a17ee6241c.text: Kate's bookcase. Arranged by subject. Pete's books are arranged by where he dropped them.

vo-746d4c2218.speaker: VO
vo-746d4c2218.text: Pete and Kate on their wedding day. Pete's grinning like he got away with something. He did.

vo-c8cc1551c6.speaker: VO
vo-c8cc1551c6.text: The air shaft. Pete calls it "the view". Pete calls a lot of things a lot of things.

vo-bbbf4ea603.speaker: VO
vo-bbbf4ea603.text: Pete Duckerton, crime reporter. Thirty-five going on fifteen. Hat on the back of his head, even indoors.

vo-92693ba75d.speaker: VO
vo-92693ba75d.text: Giving Pete back his own cigarettes would be the most honest thing I'd done all week. And the least useful.

pete-7b1bbb6cac.speaker: PETE
pete-7b1bbb6cac.text: Not if I see you first. That's journalism.

pete-92d5d00dba.speaker: PETE
pete-92d5d00dba.text: Depends. You want the news, or the news they let me print?

matt-f95a5d19ae.speaker: MATT
matt-f95a5d19ae.text: The second one. I'm short on time.

pete-a00d958430.speaker: PETE
pete-a00d958430.text: Somebody turned over Lee Wing's tea house Tuesday night. Didn't touch the till. Took his account book.

pete-af75806316.speaker: PETE
pete-af75806316.text: Thirty years of who owes Lee Wing what. In Chinatown, that's not a book. That's a map.

vo-3c8edd4a74.speaker: VO
vo-3c8edd4a74.text: Lee Wing owned the tea house, two tenements on Doyers Street, mine included, and my overdue rent. A man who got his book back might forget a few dollars.

pete-36413eb40f.speaker: PETE
pete-36413eb40f.text: Tong business, mark my words. "Blood on Doyers Street." I can see the headline.

kate-1f5365d0b4.speaker: KATE
kate-1f5365d0b4.text: Pete, a story isn't true because it's exciting. It's true because it adds up.

pete-65e2f5e3ae.speaker: PETE
pete-65e2f5e3ae.text: That's why I married her. Somebody's got to do the arithmetic.

pete-8c3b8dba2f.speaker: PETE
pete-8c3b8dba2f.text: Somebody who can't read Chinese and thought it looked expensive. Brass clasp. Nice cloth.

pete-2c7f5cf5e6.speaker: PETE
pete-2c7f5cf5e6.text: A thing like that ends up on the Bowery by breakfast. Sol Abramowitz takes anything with a hinge.

matt-bbbae6c011.speaker: MATT
matt-bbbae6c011.text: And Sol takes it in exchange for a ticket.

pete-498a130d39.speaker: PETE
pete-498a130d39.text: And forgets the face. Sol's got a memory like a sieve, and it's a very expensive sieve.

pete-1e5a0ca0b7.speaker: PETE
pete-1e5a0ca0b7.text: Love to. Can't. Kate's rationing me.

pete-de15f1de02.speaker: PETE
pete-de15f1de02.text: One pack a week, left on the table where I can see it. It's psychological warfare, Matt.

vo-2c143e3aac.speaker: VO
vo-2c143e3aac.text: If I was going to the Bowery broke, I needed something to trade. On the Bowery, cigarettes are money that burns.

pete-bd456a062b.speaker: PETE
pete-bd456a062b.text: Clarion's cutting staff. Every week another desk goes quiet. I'm writing twice as much so they can't hear mine.

pete-201dcc5d3c.speaker: PETE
pete-201dcc5d3c.text: And there's a fella on the Bowery who thinks I owe him money.

pete-b22fa420a7.speaker: PETE
pete-b22fa420a7.text: So. You walked out on the Clarion wake before the second bottle. Where'd you get to?

pete-70cc13af4f.speaker: PETE
pete-70cc13af4f.text: All three? In one night? You'll strain something.

vo-151aeae40b.speaker: VO
vo-151aeae40b.text: Pete let it go. Pete always lets it go. That's what makes him dangerous to lie to.

matt-56f02fa4c1.speaker: MATT
matt-56f02fa4c1.text: A place in the Village. There was a piano player.

pete-af3f20efdf.speaker: PETE
pete-af3f20efdf.text: Then go back and tell him so. Life's short, and the rent's due either way.

vo-f5f60bfe82.speaker: VO
vo-f5f60bfe82.text: Pete's known for years. He's never once made it a thing. It's the one room in New York where I take my hat off.

vo-aa48dd7672.speaker: VO
vo-aa48dd7672.text: Kate Duckerton. Accountant. The only person in this building who knows what day it is and what it costs.

kate-07e4be3397.speaker: KATE
kate-07e4be3397.text: Don't wave those at me, Matthew. They're evidence.

kate-e3c596f4df.speaker: KATE
kate-e3c596f4df.text: You always do. Drink your coffee first, it's paid for.

kate-f7b5a8289f.speaker: KATE
kate-f7b5a8289f.text: Head of accounts, if the board can bring themselves to say "Mrs." in a meeting. They're practising.

matt-b8f2e4b3a1.speaker: MATT
matt-b8f2e4b3a1.text: First woman to run the numbers.

kate-89eda67dc3.speaker: KATE
kate-89eda67dc3.text: First woman to be blamed for them. I'm under no illusions.

kate-17bacaabd1.speaker: KATE
kate-17bacaabd1.text: You were going to. You have your asking face on.

matt-799721a674.speaker: MATT
matt-799721a674.text: It's for a good cause. Mine.

kate-1310161a65.speaker: KATE
kate-1310161a65.text: That's not a cause, Matthew. That's a symptom.

pete-0f4eb39e82.speaker: PETE
pete-0f4eb39e82.text: I want a lot of things.

kate-d8e477cacb.speaker: KATE
kate-d8e477cacb.text: He does. It's his most consistent quality.

matt-e80898427b.speaker: MATT
matt-e80898427b.text: Think of it as an investment. I trade the smokes for Lee Wing's book, Lee forgets the rent, you keep your neighbour.

kate-ab5a8a32af.speaker: KATE
kate-ab5a8a32af.text: Sound reasoning. Badly dressed, but sound.

kate-42b2147202.speaker: KATE
kate-42b2147202.text: And I'm late. Some of us work with facts.

vo-507ccbbe1e.speaker: VO
vo-507ccbbe1e.text: Kate left. The flat got bigger and less sensible.

kate-bad082f1fd.speaker: KATE
kate-bad082f1fd.text: I'll be here. Not giving you Pete's cigarettes.

vo-1276e43fc1.speaker: VO
vo-1276e43fc1.text: Doyers Street. One bend, three hundred feet, and a reputation it earned the hard way.

vo-50074e6e17.speaker: VO
vo-50074e6e17.text: Laundry, lanterns and steam. Chinatown keeps its secrets warm.

vo-558945b3d9.speaker: VO
vo-558945b3d9.text: Better leave that where it is. Things on this street belong to somebody.

vo-d2eb50a5a3.speaker: VO
vo-d2eb50a5a3.text: Lee Wing's tea house. Lee owns it, the tenement across the street where I live, and one more besides. And my rent.

vo-dda082c0af.speaker: VO
vo-dda082c0af.text: Three brass balls. Two to one you won't get it back.

vo-3140a23bca.speaker: VO
vo-3140a23bca.text: Other people's lives in a window, at a reasonable rate of interest.

vo-457157c96a.speaker: VO
vo-457157c96a.text: The kid sells the Clarion on this corner every morning. Pete tips him a nickel to shout his headlines louder.

matt-725e21c763.speaker: MATT
matt-725e21c763.text: I've got a friend who writes it. I get it for free and it still costs me.

newsboy-92d829bd14.speaker: NEWSBOY
newsboy-92d829bd14.text: Then you owe me two cents for the joke.

vo-9973c6546c.speaker: VO
vo-9973c6546c.text: The far end opens onto the Bowery and the rest of the city. The rest of the city can wait until I can afford it.

vo-834e8611c4.speaker: VO
vo-834e8611c4.text: Somebody's long johns, frozen stiff. It's going to be that kind of winter.

vo-ecced65e9c.speaker: VO
vo-ecced65e9c.text: Lacquer, smoke and an abacus that never stops counting.

vo-4c72b7c5b7.speaker: VO
vo-4c72b7c5b7.text: Lee Wing's tea house. Quiet as a church, if a church kept accounts.

vo-fa785191e0.speaker: VO
vo-fa785191e0.text: Lee's things stay where Lee puts them.

vo-6e5b6dacab.speaker: VO
vo-6e5b6dacab.text: Lee Wing. My landlord. He knows what everybody on Doyers Street owes, to the penny and the favour.

lee-e35ec1071c.speaker: LEE
lee-e35ec1071c.text: I don't smoke, Mr. Long. It shortens the memory.

lee-5d03cde698.speaker: LEE
lee-5d03cde698.text: Mr. Long. You read my letter.

lee-188d68ddd1.speaker: LEE
lee-188d68ddd1.text: Mr. Long. Someone has taken my account book. Thirty years of names. I would like it back... before anybody reads it.

matt-a335ef84c2.speaker: MATT
matt-a335ef84c2.text: You want me to find it.

lee-f2c8b895a5.speaker: LEE
lee-f2c8b895a5.text: I want it on my counter. How it gets there is your business. You have a business, I think. It says so on your door.

lee-8d41de4b23.speaker: LEE
lee-8d41de4b23.text: Bring the book, and the rent can wait two weeks.

lee-f22dfda8b3.speaker: LEE
lee-f22dfda8b3.text: A roof. It is snowing, Mr. Long.

vo-7367543de2.speaker: VO
vo-7367543de2.text: A thin boy, a big coat, and the Bowery. That narrowed it down to half the Bowery.

lee-5f5dd6fd09.speaker: LEE
lee-5f5dd6fd09.text: The book, Mr. Long. My counter. Two weeks.

vo-859e6421ab.speaker: VO
vo-859e6421ab.text: Cages of other people's lives, and a dim bulb to read the price by.

vo-ac87b2e051.speaker: VO
vo-ac87b2e051.text: Every object in here was somebody's last good idea.

sol-9e06b410bc.speaker: SOL
sol-9e06b410bc.text: You break it, you bought it. You look at it, I'm watching.

vo-6d44d24b1b.speaker: VO
vo-6d44d24b1b.text: The back door. Out to the alley, where the Bowery keeps what it doesn't want seen.

vo-7fac2fbb8d.speaker: VO
vo-7fac2fbb8d.text: Sol's ticket ledger. Every pledge in the shop, in a hand so small it's practically a secret.

sol-51a48735a9.speaker: SOL
sol-51a48735a9.text: Hands off the ledger, mister. That's not reading material, that's my livelihood.

vo-178bc009bb.speaker: VO
vo-178bc009bb.text: Behind the wire, a cloth-bound book with Chinese on the cover. It looked lonely among the saxophones.

vo-8b21e96220.speaker: VO
vo-8b21e96220.text: Fifty clocks, all telling a different time. On the Bowery, that's about right.

vo-dd4ae41fb8.speaker: VO
vo-dd4ae41fb8.text: Violins. You pawn the violin when the band's let you go. You pawn the case when you've stopped hoping.

vo-23a08d94f3.speaker: VO
vo-23a08d94f3.text: Sol Abramowitz. He's seen every hard-luck story on the Bowery, and he gave most of them a ticket.

sol-206733717c.speaker: SOL
sol-206733717c.text: I look like a tobacconist? I look like a man with a cold. Keep your cigarettes.

sol-c1f1093bb4.speaker: SOL
sol-c1f1093bb4.text: At this hour? Put it away, I'm a respectable crook.

matt-bc3e408335.speaker: MATT
matt-bc3e408335.text: You've got a book back there. Cloth cover, Chinese writing. It belongs to Lee Wing.

sol-04d631c006.speaker: SOL
sol-04d631c006.text: Everything in this shop has a ticket, mister. No ticket, no story. And believe me... I've heard all the stories.

sol-c2e097f552.speaker: SOL
sol-c2e097f552.text: A customer. They all look the same from this side of the counter. Hungry.

sol-7a17cb84aa.speaker: SOL
sol-7a17cb84aa.text: This one, maybe hungrier. He went out the back. They like the back.

matt-7366ff8a65.speaker: MATT
matt-7366ff8a65.text: Lee Wing won't like you holding his book for ransom.

sol-df783e8781.speaker: SOL
sol-df783e8781.text: Ransom? It's a loan, sixty cents, all legal. Tell Lee Wing I kept it dry. Tell him I didn't open it.

vo-0480fcb5fd.speaker: VO
vo-0480fcb5fd.text: Sol was scared of Lee Wing. Sol is not scared of much. I filed that away.

sol-a93abcf0ee.speaker: SOL
sol-a93abcf0ee.text: Looking is free. Looking long is a nickel.

sol-0c6a958124.speaker: SOL
sol-0c6a958124.text: Four-four-one-seven. A book, cloth, one. Sixty cents, the loan and the interest.

sol-da6225e1cd.speaker: SOL
sol-da6225e1cd.text: So skip lunch. You look like a man who's had practice.

vo-6bb175778c.speaker: VO
vo-6bb175778c.text: Sixty cents lighter, I had Lee Wing's book. It was heavier than it looked. Most books with names in are.

sol-6b0f0bc910.speaker: SOL
sol-6b0f0bc910.text: You again. You want something else of somebody's? I got a trumpet, barely used. The fella barely could play.

vo-ef3511a457.speaker: VO
vo-ef3511a457.text: The alley behind Sol's. The Bowery's back pocket.

vo-4c379a49cb.speaker: VO
vo-4c379a49cb.text: Wet brick, wet rags, and a smell like the city's been sick in its sleep.

vo-29306ff2d2.speaker: VO
vo-29306ff2d2.text: Whatever's in there can stay in there.

vo-4716fca7b1.speaker: VO
vo-4716fca7b1.text: Rags and newspapers. Somebody's bed. Somebody's whole estate.

vo-0e259051f3.speaker: VO
vo-0e259051f3.text: A thin kid in a coat too big for him. Shaking, and not only from the cold.

junkie-84cdde2a32.speaker: JUNKIE
junkie-84cdde2a32.text: Ain't drinkin' it. I want somethin' I can sell.

vo-1795972f57.speaker: VO
vo-1795972f57.text: Fair enough. I wasn't keen to part with it either.

junkie-9b589f1b89.speaker: JUNKIE
junkie-9b589f1b89.text: Whatever it is, I didn't do it. And if I did, it was somebody else.

matt-2ee75e2deb.speaker: MATT
matt-2ee75e2deb.text: You pawned a book at Sol's. Cloth cover, Chinese on it.

junkie-2a1607c7aa.speaker: JUNKIE
junkie-2a1607c7aa.text: Ticket? Yeah, I got a ticket. What's it to you? A pack. Make it two packs, pal, and it's yours.

vo-7e1e6646de.speaker: VO
vo-7e1e6646de.text: Two packs. I had one, and it was Kate's.

vo-40cc2a2d52.speaker: VO
vo-40cc2a2d52.text: I didn't have one pack, let alone two.

junkie-6d1f4d32a6.speaker: JUNKIE
junkie-6d1f4d32a6.text: You look like a cop. We both got problems.

junkie-22027eb86f.speaker: JUNKIE
junkie-22027eb86f.text: Smokes? What for? What do you want?

vo-080a9fdd38.speaker: VO
vo-080a9fdd38.text: Better find out what he's got before I hand over the only currency I own.

matt-dda06fd805.speaker: MATT
matt-dda06fd805.text: One pack. Take it or don't.

vo-7d1dac6bb6.speaker: VO
vo-7d1dac6bb6.text: Pawn ticket four-four-one-seven, warm from his pocket.

matt-2ec8f8ca12.speaker: MATT
matt-2ec8f8ca12.text: Lee Wing knows a thin boy in a big coat took it. Find another street for a while.

vo-84295c89ab.speaker: VO
vo-84295c89ab.text: He didn't say thanks. I didn't expect it. Warnings are like that.

vo-2a228e770f.speaker: VO
vo-2a228e770f.text: I let it lie. Lee Wing would find him or he wouldn't. Neither one was my rent.

matt-079c41c485.speaker: MATT
matt-079c41c485.text: One account book. Thirty years of names, sixty cents of interest. I didn't read it.

lee-12e02a357f.speaker: LEE
lee-12e02a357f.text: That is better than not reading it.

lee-a3165fee22.speaker: LEE
lee-a3165fee22.text: Two weeks, Mr. Long. Then we talk again about the rent.

matt-5f382098b3.speaker: MATT
matt-5f382098b3.text: The kid who took it sleeps behind Sol's, in the alley.

lee-e697c763b6.speaker: LEE
lee-e697c763b6.text: I know where he sleeps. I wanted to know if you would tell me.

vo-55d44e7e58.speaker: VO
vo-55d44e7e58.text: I'd passed some kind of test. I wasn't sure which side of it I'd come out on.

matt-ea1afc83f2.speaker: MATT
matt-ea1afc83f2.text: I never got a good look at him.

lee-403121d673.speaker: LEE
lee-403121d673.text: No. Nobody does, on the Bowery.

vo-022c5b50ce.speaker: VO
vo-022c5b50ce.text: He knew. Lee always knows. He let me keep the lie, which on Doyers Street is a kind of favour.

vo-5cd9443e19.speaker: VO
vo-5cd9443e19.text: Two weeks' grace. On Doyers Street that's practically a pension.

lee-036fe20454.speaker: LEE
lee-036fe20454.text: Two weeks, Mr. Long. I have written it down. You know how I am with books.

vo-648251f8c2.speaker: VO
vo-648251f8c2.text: The snow turned to rain by dark. I sat in the office and let it explain things to the window.

vo-b129153e6b.speaker: VO
vo-b129153e6b.text: Two weeks' grace and forty-odd cents. I was doing the sums again when the knock came.

vo-d01bdc9e34.speaker: VO
vo-d01bdc9e34.text: She came in out of the rain like she'd paid it to stop.

vo-124d07f84e.speaker: VO
vo-124d07f84e.text: Platinum hair, dark eyes, a fur collar. The coat had been mended at one cuff. Rich people don't mend. They replace.

inez-3151955ffe.speaker: INEZ
inez-3151955ffe.text: They tell me you find people, Mr. Long. I need you to find one man. Quietly.

inez-e71f6f5079.speaker: INEZ
inez-e71f6f5079.text: Captain Michael Harlan. Army Medical Corps. He's a surgeon on Governors Island.

vo-9af9b06139.speaker: VO
vo-9af9b06139.text: She slid a photograph across the desk. Square jaw, Army collar, the kind of face they put on recruiting posters.

inez-6b2ada87e9.speaker: INEZ
inez-6b2ada87e9.text: He hates the parades. He said he'd come to dinner after. He didn't come.

inez-57aa5eaf54.speaker: INEZ
inez-57aa5eaf54.text: That he's on leave. Michael has never taken a day's leave in his life. He wouldn't know what to do with it.

inez-8d79affc71.speaker: INEZ
inez-8d79affc71.text: A detective wrote "lovers' quarrel" in his notebook and offered me his handkerchief.

inez-9e4d617a71.speaker: INEZ
inez-9e4d617a71.text: Because you used to be a policeman, Mr. Long, and you aren't any more. Those are both recommendations.

vo-1b6cd1cf50.speaker: VO
vo-1b6cd1cf50.text: She'd done her homework. I wondered who'd marked it.

matt-e0bce056b6.speaker: MATT
matt-e0bce056b6.text: Men walk out, Miss Venta. Some of them even mean it.

inez-15af7f7e95.speaker: INEZ
inez-15af7f7e95.text: Then find him and let him tell me so. I'd like to hear it in his voice.

vo-1ecbf46211.speaker: VO
vo-1ecbf46211.text: A society girl and a missing boyfriend. A routine job. I'd done a dozen. I told myself this was the thirteenth.

inez-9e89f29615.speaker: INEZ
inez-9e89f29615.text: Fifty dollars, Mr. Long. In advance.

vo-7e4f5bf5b2.speaker: VO
vo-7e4f5bf5b2.text: Fifty dollars. Two months' rent, to the penny. Lee Wing would be delighted, and suspicious.

vo-9f14c3ce03.speaker: VO
vo-9f14c3ce03.text: She left the way she came: like the rain was hers, and she was lending it to me.

vo-0ca159e2f3.speaker: VO
vo-0ca159e2f3.text: I took out the notebook. A man who forgets what people tell him ends up believing what they meant.

vo-6bda038445.speaker: VO
vo-6bda038445.text: The board. Old cases on the edges. Room in the middle for a new one.

vo-3c0112596c.speaker: VO
vo-3c0112596c.text: Captain Michael Harlan, pinned in the middle where I can see him.

vo-2ce3492df1.speaker: VO
vo-2ce3492df1.text: The key to his front door. A door nobody's answered in nine days.

vo-2eafe3576c.speaker: VO
vo-2eafe3576c.text: A man who never takes leave is "on leave" for nine days, and the Army's not worried. Somebody is lying, or somebody's been told to.

vo-23d1c21853.speaker: VO
vo-23d1c21853.text: Start where he lived. Keys open more than doors.

vo-628487e275.speaker: VO
vo-628487e275.text: "Notice to quit." Lee Wing's English is better than mine when there's money in it.

vo-321fc45d99.speaker: VO
vo-321fc45d99.text: My flask. Half full, or half empty, depending on the hour.

vo-619b0bcaa9.speaker: VO
vo-619b0bcaa9.text: Pete's cigarettes, a Bowery brand. Kate's ration, Pete's ransom, my currency.

vo-5eb0a8ec5a.speaker: VO
vo-5eb0a8ec5a.text: Ticket four-four-one-seven. A card that says somebody else owns a piece of your life.

vo-ba547fc39c.speaker: VO
vo-ba547fc39c.text: Lee Wing's account book. I don't read Chinese, and tonight's not the night to learn.

vo-c6dc549496.speaker: VO
vo-c6dc549496.text: Fifty dollars. The rent, the grocer, and a week of not answering the door.

vo-e1faf4fde2.speaker: VO
vo-e1faf4fde2.text: Captain Michael Harlan, Medical Corps. Steady eyes. The kind of man who doesn't go missing by accident.

vo-1ab7eba946.speaker: VO
vo-1ab7eba946.text: His door key. West Eighty-Fourth Street. A key to a door nobody's answered in nine days.

vo-db5fe54490.speaker: VO
vo-db5fe54490.text: I tried it in my head first. It didn't work there either.

inez-6733d30d82.speaker: INEZ
inez-6733d30d82.text: And this. The key to his apartment. West Eighty-Fourth Street.

vo-4022339bd7.speaker: VO
vo-4022339bd7.text: One cup is hospitality. Two is a loan.

vo-2b2244ff9b.speaker: VO
vo-2b2244ff9b.text: I had Kate's cup in my pocket. All it needed was to go under the spout.

vo-9c2dbd0d30.speaker: VO
vo-9c2dbd0d30.text: I'd need a cup. There's a clean one on the table. Kate lays one out for whoever turns up. Usually it's me.

vo-548bd933cd.speaker: VO
vo-548bd933cd.text: A clean cup on a saucer, set out for whoever turns up. Usually it's me.

vo-2ab2de1c27.speaker: VO
vo-2ab2de1c27.text: I took the cup. Kate would know. Kate always knows.

kate-3b35793bd2.speaker: KATE
kate-3b35793bd2.text: It's clean, Matt. Bring it back that way.

vo-bc6e0cda7b.speaker: VO
vo-bc6e0cda7b.text: Today's Clarion, folded to Pete's page. Kate reads it from the front, Pete from his own byline.

vo-2b2b2ac2c8.speaker: VO
vo-2b2b2ac2c8.text: "Crater Still Missing." A Supreme Court justice hails a cab on West Forty-Fifth Street in August and is never seen again. Three months, and the police have a reward poster and a shrug.

vo-1f778c6a3b.speaker: VO
vo-1f778c6a3b.text: "Seabury Widens Magistrates' Inquiry." Talk of vice cops framing women in the Women's Court, and bondsmen splitting the bail. Somewhere in this city, a detective is wondering if his name comes up next.

vo-f23e08e892.speaker: VO
vo-f23e08e892.text: "Apple Sellers on Every Corner." The growers' association sells them a crate on credit, and they sell the apples at a nickel each. Six thousand men with a box and a tie. I counted two of them on my block who used to be bankers.

vo-0054861a90.speaker: VO
vo-0054861a90.text: "Roosevelt Re-Elected by Record Margin." The governor wins by seven hundred thousand votes. Tammany is pleased. When Tammany is pleased, somebody else is paying.

vo-4b27f688d4.speaker: VO
vo-4b27f688d4.text: "Legs Diamond Will Live, Doctors Say." Shot five times at the Hotel Monticello last month, and still breathing. They haven't made the bullet that can find his heart. Nobody's sure he has one.

vo-04a6dce2cb.speaker: VO
vo-04a6dce2cb.text: "Mooring Mast Rises Atop Empire State." A dock for airships, a quarter of a mile above Fifth Avenue. The city can't pay its rent, but it can build a ladder to heaven.

vo-a9b7f53500.speaker: VO
vo-a9b7f53500.text: "Half a Million Out of Work in City." The Prosser committee asks everyone with a job to give a day's pay. Most people I know haven't had a day's pay to give since summer.

vo-f891ec3464.speaker: VO
vo-f891ec3464.text: Kate's spare cup. Good china, meaning it hasn't broken yet.

lee-1043e9fea9.speaker: LEE
lee-1043e9fea9.text: A boy was seen running toward the Bowery. Thin. A coat too big for him.

lee-ac52fbe028.speaker: LEE
lee-ac52fbe028.text: Slow business makes a man available, Mr. Long. I will remember that you are available.

vo-a7cbca739f.speaker: VO
vo-a7cbca739f.text: Off. The bad news can wait. It always does.

vo-20949fef46.speaker: VO
vo-20949fef46.text: Quiet. The city can tell me the rest tomorrow.

vo-c08cba422f.speaker: VO
vo-c08cba422f.text: WMCA, from the roof of the Hotel McAlpin. The news, and records older than my debts.

vo-0849a6928d.speaker: VO
vo-0849a6928d.text: The radio. Company that doesn't ask for a retainer.
